Fit a Royle-Nichols occupancy model with false positives

Source: R/fp_occu_rn.R
fp_occu_rn.Rd

Fits the abundance-induced heterogeneity model of Royle and Nichols (2003) with false positives in Stan. The number of individuals at site \(i\) is \(N_i \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i)\), each detected on an occasion with probability \(r\), so the automated method detects the species with probability \(1 - (1 - r)^{N_i}\), and the site is occupied when \(N_i > 0\). A site effect on \(r\) (random_det) then measures variation in detection among sites beyond that due to abundance, which fp_occu() cannot separate from it.

Usage

fp_occu_rn(
  data,
  occ = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  random_recorder = !is.null(data$recorder),
  ver = ~1,
  random_fp = FALSE,
  random_det = FALSE,
  random_abund = FALSE,
  n_max = 20,
  priors = fp_priors(),
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = chains,
  threads_per_chain = "auto",
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  adapt_delta = 0.99,
  seed = NULL,
  refresh = NULL,
  prior_only = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

An fp_data object from fp_data(), fp_data_wide(), or simulate_fp().

occ

One-sided formula for log abundance (\(\log \lambda\)); site covariates only. The occupancy probability is \(\psi = 1 - e^{-\lambda}\).

det

One-sided formula for the logit of the per-individual detection \(r\) of the automated method (site or occasion covariates).

fp

One-sided formula for the logit of the false-positive rate, or NULL for the Royle-Nichols model without false positives. Site covariates only.

random_recorder

Logical. Add a recorder random intercept to true detection? Defaults to TRUE when data has a recorder column. Data from simulate_fp() always have one; with its default sd_recorder = 0 set this to FALSE, because a random effect whose true variance is zero causes divergent transitions.

ver

One-sided formula for the logit of the per-individual detection of the verified method.

random_fp

Logical. Add a site random intercept to the logit of the false-positive rate.

random_det

Logical. Add a site random intercept to the logit of the per-individual detection \(r\): its standard deviation (sd_det_site) is the variation in detection among sites that abundance does not explain.

random_abund

Logical. Add a site random intercept to log abundance (sd_abund_site), for variation in abundance beyond the covariates of occ.

n_max

Largest abundance summed over. The fit warns when the Poisson mass above it is not negligible at some site.

priors

Prior settings from fp_priors().

chains, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, adapt_delta, seed

Single numbers (seed may be NULL), checked before sampling and passed to the $sample() method of 'cmdstanr', which runs Stan's No-U-Turn sampler (Hoffman & Gelman, 2014). chains is the number of Markov chains (4 by default); iter_warmup and iter_sampling are the warm-up and kept iterations of each chain (1000 each); warm-up draws adapt the sampler and are discarded. adapt_delta is the target acceptance rate during adaptation (0.95, above the Stan default of 0.8, because the false-positive models often have curved posteriors); raise it towards 0.99 when divergent transitions are reported. seed is the random seed; with NULL, CmdStan draws one, and the seed used is stored in $sampler$seed either way.

parallel_chains

Number of chains run in parallel.

threads_per_chain

Number of threads each chain uses to compute the likelihood, which is summed over sites in parallel with Stan's reduce_sum(). One of:

  • "auto": the physical cores divided among the parallel chains of this fit (not among other processes, such as calibration workers). The fastest choice for most data, but a fit is not reproduced exactly by its seed: with more than one thread the partial sums are added in an order that varies from run to run, so the draws drift apart after a while. The posterior is the same.

  • 1: each chain runs on one core, and the same seed gives the same draws. Use it when exact reproduction matters (published analyses, tests, saved results).

  • a larger number: that many threads per chain, with the same caveat as "auto". Keep parallel_chains * threads_per_chain at or below the number of cores.

Threads speed up fits with many sites or occasions (on the curiango data, 4 threads made each chain 3.4 times faster). The default is "auto" since crywolf 2.0.0 (it was 1 before). Under R CMD check (when _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ is set, as on CRAN) a fit uses at most two cores, counting parallel_chains * threads_per_chain.

refresh

How often each chain reports its progress, in iterations. The default, NULL, reports every 10% of the iterations in interactive sessions and nothing otherwise; 0 silences it. Warm-up iterations are usually slower than sampling ones, so the first half of the run takes more than half of the time.

prior_only

Logical. If TRUE, the likelihood is left out and the sampler draws from the priors alone, through the same Stan program. This checks what the priors imply and that the sampler recovers them; fp_prior_predictive() gives the prior predictive distribution without CmdStan.

...

Further arguments passed to the $sample() method of 'cmdstanr', for example max_treedepth, show_messages = FALSE and show_exceptions = FALSE (with refresh = 0, a silent run), save_warmup = TRUE (so that plot(fit, type = "trace") shows the warm-up), or init. init takes starting values (a number, a list per chain, or a function), or a previous fit, init = old$fit, so that a run starts where an earlier one ended; the draws of the earlier run are not pooled with the new ones. Only Stan's No-U-Turn sampler is offered.

Value

An object of class fp_occu_rn, with the elements of an fp_occu() fit (fit, draws, stan_data, formulas, design, data, priors, sampler, diagnostics, call) and n_max. The draws hold the abundance coefficients (abund_*), the detection coefficients on the logit of \(r\) (det_*), the false-positive intercept and slopes, the verified detection, the derived quantities lambda_ref and psi_ref (at the reference of the covariates), lambda_bar and psi_bar (means over sites), r_ref, p10_ref and r_verified, and the standard deviations of the site effects.

Details

Model. With \(N_i \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i)\), $$\log \lambda_i = X_i \beta \; [+ v_i],$$ an automated occasion \(k\) of site \(i\) is a detection with probability $$1 - (1 - r_{ik})^{N_i} (1 - p_{10,i}),$$ $$\mathrm{logit}(r_{ik}) = Z_{ik} \alpha + u_{\mathrm{rec}[ik]} \; [+ d_i],$$ $$\mathrm{logit}(p_{10,i}) = \gamma_0 + X^{fp}_i \gamma \; [+ e_i],$$ so false positives occur on every occasion, also at occupied sites, and an unoccupied site (\(N_i = 0\)) is detected with probability \(p_{10,i}\). A verified occasion is a detection with probability \(1 - (1 - r^{v})^{N_i}\). The site effects \(v_i\), \(d_i\) and \(e_i\) are normal with standard deviations sd_abund_site, sd_det_site and sd_fp_site and half-normal priors (abund_site_sd, det_site_sd and fp_site_sd of fp_priors()). Unlike fp_occu(), the false-positive intercept \(\gamma_0\) is not tied to the detection intercept by a gap: detection at an occupied site always exceeds \(p_{10}\), so the labels cannot switch, and \(p_{10}\) may exceed the per-individual detection \(r\). Its prior is the marginal prior the gap implies in fp_occu(): Normal with mean -gap_mean and standard deviation sqrt(intercept_sd^2 + gap_sd^2). \(N_i\) is summed out over 0 to n_max.

Observation-confirmation design. Confirmed occasions (argument confirmed of fp_data()) enter as in fp_occu(), with probabilities of at least one true observation \(s_1 = 1 - (1 - r)^{N_i}\) and at least one false observation \(s_0 = p_{10}\). They can be the same occasions as the automated detections, so a fully annotated survey enters as one row per occasion with both columns filled.

Outputs. print(), summary(), as_draws_df(), loo() (leave one site out), simulate() (new abundances and detections with the design of the data) and fp_sites() and fp_ppc(), which use the posterior of each site's abundance given its data; see fp_occu_rn-methods.

Not supported. False-positive covariates measured on each occasion, runs of detections (markov of fp_occu()), and the other outputs of fp_occu() (predict(), coef(), fp_effects(), plot()).

Identifiability. In simulations (vignette("royle-nichols"), code in dev/rn-fp/ of the package repository), the power to detect sd_det_site = 1 grew with the number of sites and occasions, from about half at 25 sites and 10 occasions to above 90% at 100 sites and 20 occasions, and depended little on whether verified data or confirmed occasions supplied the information. sd_abund_site was weakly identified. With few sites the prior of sd_det_site carries much of the posterior near 0: compare fits under several values of det_site_sd. The default adapt_delta is 0.99, above the 0.95 of fp_occu(): the site effects create funnels, and at 0.95 most simulated designs had divergences. With many sites, also use longer chains than the default: the standard deviations of the site effects mix slowly.

References

Royle, J. A. and Nichols, J. D. (2003). Estimating abundance from repeated presence-absence data or point counts. Ecology, 84, 777–790. doi:10.1890/0012-9658(2003)084[0777:EAFRPA]2.0.CO;2

Chambert, T., Miller, D. A. W. and Nichols, J. D. (2015). Modeling false positive detections in species occurrence data under different study designs. Ecology, 96, 332–339. doi:10.1890/14-1507.1

See also

simulate_fp_rn(), fp_occu()

Examples

# \donttest{
s <- simulate_fp_rn(nsite = 60, nocc = 10, sigma_r = 1, seed = 1)
m <- fp_occu_rn(s$data, random_det = TRUE, chains = 2,
                iter_warmup = 300, iter_sampling = 300, seed = 1)
